subject: Load-sculpting experiment logistics and evidence delivery
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimbusfin.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial scope: load-sculpting experiments and evidence needs

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday. Nimbus is trying to validate vendor behavior under realistic surge and burst scenarios for an upcoming production rollout. Before we schedule the lab, can you share a concise survey of how Redwood would run the following:

- Controlled burst tests (sub-minute spikes up to 30x baseline)
- Sustained concurrency increments (1x -> 50x over incremental windows)
- Cold-start vs warm-start latency windows and how you instrument them

We also need a short list of the artifacts you can deliver after a run (raw latency quantiles, GPU utilization traces, kernel-selection logs, per-replica token throughput, and the test harness scripts). Attached is a CSV with our approximate traffic mix (synth-load-specs.csv) — it includes sequence-length distribution, percent chat-type requests, and a small-weighted long-tail set.

Procurement note: we have a tentative acceptance window in mid-November; providing a clear, reproducible test plan + artifacts will speed the procurement sign-off.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) run a 48-hour soak with intermittent microbursts for validation;
2) provide the run scripts and a short runbook we can replay locally; and
3) annotate any fallbacks you use (model-fanout, regional routing, admission-control) so our SREs can evaluate integration impact.

Thanks,

Elena Soto
Principal Platform Engineer
Nimbus Financial

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimbusfin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial scope: load-sculpting experiments and evidence needs

Elena — thanks for the clear list and the CSV. Attached is a short protocol (rfi-load-protocol-v1.docx) that outlines the baseline configuration we propose for Nimbus and the artifacts we'll commit to share. High level summary below.

TL;DR: Yes — we can run a 48-hour soak with scheduled microbursts and provide reproducible scripts and artifacts. We recommend a two-phase lab: (A) reproduction of your traffic mix at steady state, then (B) a controlled burst window and degradation/fallback observation.

Planned test matrix (summary):
- Models: open/gpt-7b-quant (primary), open/gpt-7b-quant-lowmem (fallback)
- Concurrency sweep: 10 -> 500 concurrent requests (step 10x, 25x, 50x)
- Burst tests: synthetic spikes of 10s / 60s / 300s at 10x, 20x, 30x multipliers over baseline
- Sequence lengths: sample buckets at 16, 64, 256, 1024 tokens (weighted by your CSV)
- Warmup: 15-minute prefix traffic to populate KV caches + two full model forward passes per replica
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (per-token and end-to-end), avg tokens/sec, GPU/CPU utilization, memory/RTX allocator traces, backend queue depth, and kernel selection logs
- Failure injection: optional (network hiccup, replica kill) to show graceful fallback behavior

Instrumentation & harness: we use k6 for traffic shaping and an internal traffic-generator that emits tokenized request traces. We capture metrics to a time-series backend and export raw traces as CSV + perf traces. We'll provide the run harness and a stripped-down example run script (run-sweep-sample.sh) you can replay.

Deliverables we will provide after the lab (per your list):
- Latency quantiles (CSV + annotated plots)
- Per-replica traces and GPU telemetry (CSV)
- Kernel-selection and quantization-profile logs (plain text)
- Run harness and example scripts (Bash + k6 config)
- A short narrative run report that highlights headroom, observed tail amplification, and recommended configuration changes

I'll let Karthik add the technical kernel/batching details below. If you're aligned, we'll propose workshop dates and reserve a lab window.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimbusfin.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: James Liu <james.liu@nimbusfin.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial scope: load-sculpting experiments and evidence needs

Grace / Karthik — this looks good. A couple clarifications before we lock workshop dates: 

1) Cold-start definition: what time window do you use to declare a request as a cold start for KV cache behavior? We want to know the window that most strongly correlates with 99th percentile blow-ups.
2) Batching guidance: will you run with a fixed batching window (e.g., 10ms) or adaptive batching based on queue depth? If adaptive, can you provide the thresholds you expect to surface in the run artifacts?
3) Reproducibility: can you produce a small artifact that shows a single-step run command we can execute (we prefer something that does not require full Redwood infra)?

Also — procurement asked whether the run report can call out exact pass/fail criteria tied to our acceptance SLO: p99 < 600ms for chat-default (64 token avg) and throughput >= 2K tokens/sec sustained across replicas. If you can annotate the run with fail flags, that will be very helpful.

Finally, we'd like a short canary plan that describes rollback behavior (if degradation is seen in production) — e.g., model-fanout to smaller quantized variant or regional failover.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimbusfin.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial scope: load-sculpting experiments and evidence needs

Elena — quick technical notes to answer your three questions and to make the run reproducible.

Cold-start window: we treat a replica as "cold" until the KV cache has been populated with a full pass for the target context window. Practically that maps to ~2x the largest sequence-length bucket in your mix (so with 1k tokens max we use a 2000-token priming window). For short-chat workloads the effective cold window is smaller; we capture cold-tagged traces for the first 10 minutes of the run for explicit analysis.

Batching: Redwood uses an adaptive batching scheduler by default. It prefers small fixed microwindows (5ms) but will grow the window up to 30ms under sustained queue depth to improve throughput. Key thresholds we expose in artifacts: queue-depth >= 8 triggers window growth; latency growth beyond p95 target will force batch-size/timeout tradeoff adjustments. We'll include the exact threshold file in kernel-selection logs.

Admission & fallback: we expose a simple admission-control policy in the run that does the following: 1) soft-throttle at per-replica queue depth 120; 2) hard-reject at queue depth 240 with a documented error code; 3) model-fanout to open/gpt-7b-quant-lowmem as an automatic fallback when per-replica GPU memory crosses 85% for >30s. Regional fallback is performed via traffic routing rules you control.

Reproducible run: see attached run-sweep-sample.sh for an end-to-end example. The script relies on k6 and our small helper (redwood-run-client) that can be built from source; we will provide a link in the Drive. The minimal invocation looks like this in bash:

  ./run-sweep-sample.sh --config synth-load-specs.csv --model open/gpt-7b-quant --duration 48h --bursts 10s,60s,300s

Pass/fail automation: we will annotate the run report with boolean flags mapped to your acceptance SLOs (p99 < 600ms on chat-default; throughput >= 2000 tokens/sec). If a flag is tripped we include the offending time window and the candidate mitigations we tried during the run.

Link to artifacts folder (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRFI-lab-artifacts

I'll coordinate the workshop tech attendees once we confirm a date.

—Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: run-sweep-sample.sh

Elena / James — great to align. Proposed next steps and responsibilities: 

1) Workshop & lab window: Redwood runs the lab Nov 16–18 (48h soak with scheduled bursts). Can you confirm a 90-minute prep workshop on Nov 15 to finalize the exact traffic CSV and any optional failure injections?
2) Deliverables: We'll upload raw artifacts to the Drive folder above and produce a 6–8 page run report within 3 business days of run completion. The report will include pass/fail flags mapped to the acceptance SLOs you provided.
3) Canary plan: we'll provide a one-page canary playbook during the workshop that covers model-fanout, admission-control tuning, and regional fallback.
4) Procurement: Karthik and I will include the artifact checklist (lab-artifacts-checklist.pdf) with the procurement packet so your legal/procurement team can validate evidence types.

If this schedule works we will reserve the lab and start pre-populating test instances with your CSV immediately. Let us know the best time on Nov 15 for the prep workshop and whether your SREs prefer UTC or PST for the session.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
